question: What type of propeller is fitted to each engine of the DA 42 NG?

options.text: A hydraulically regulated, 3-bladed, constant-speed feathering propeller (mt-Propeller MTV-6-R-C-F)
A fixed-pitch, 2-bladed wooden propeller
An electrically regulated, 3-bladed, non-feathering propeller
A hydraulically regulated, 2-bladed feathering propeller

explanation: AFM 7.9.2 describes two mt-Propeller MTV-6-R-C-F / CF 190-69 hydraulically regulated, 3-bladed, constant-speed feathering propellers.

question: What effect does INCREASING gearbox oil pressure to the propeller hub have on pitch and RPM?

options.text: Feathers the propeller immediately
Decreases pitch and increases RPM
Increases pitch and decreases RPM
Has no effect on pitch, only on RPM

explanation: AFM 7.9.2: increasing oil pressure decreases pitch and raises RPM; decreasing pressure increases pitch and lowers RPM.

question: What is the function of the pressure accumulator in the propeller system?

options.text: It stores fuel for emergency engine restart
It supplies backup electrical power to the ECU
It ensures adequate oil pressure is available even when gearbox oil pump feed decreases under negative acceleration
It cools the gearbox oil during high-power climbs

explanation: AFM 7.9.2 describes the nitrogen-oil pressure accumulator maintaining adequate propeller pitch control oil pressure during negative acceleration.

question: What opens the electric valve at the pressure accumulator?

options.text: Setting the ALTERNATOR switch to ON
Pressing the ECU TEST button
Moving the VOTER switch to AUTO
Setting the ENGINE MASTER switch to ON

explanation: AFM 7.9.2: the accumulator's electric valve is controlled by the ENGINE MASTER switch — ON opens it, connecting it to the gearbox oil circuit.

question: What happens to the propeller blades if the engine is shut down (ENGINE MASTER OFF) at a propeller speed BELOW 1300 RPM?

options.text: The propeller pitch remains below the start-lock position, and speed must be increased to feather correctly
The propeller feathers normally regardless of RPM
The propeller automatically unfeathers again
Nothing unusual happens — feathering always completes below 1300 RPM

explanation: AFM 7.9.2 cautions that feathering below 1300 RPM leaves the pitch below the start-lock position, requiring an RPM increase to correct it.

question: During unfeathering, what supplies the initial oil pressure that moves the propeller blades to a low pitch position, before the gearbox oil pump takes over?

options.text: The turbocharger oil supply
The pressure accumulator
The ECU backup battery, via an electric actuator
The main engine oil pump

explanation: AFM 7.9.2: unfeathering opens the accumulator's electric valve, and its stored pressure moves the blades to low pitch until the gearbox oil pump takes over as the propeller starts turning.

question: Why should ground operation at high RPM be avoided where possible?

options.text: It causes excessive ECU cycling between channels
It drains the ECU backup batteries
The wooden composite propeller blades could suffer stone damage
High RPM on the ground overheats the gearbox oil

explanation: AFM 7.9.2 recommends selecting a suitable ground-run site free of loose stones, since the blades could suffer stone damage at high RPM.

question: What sets the propeller pitch according to the ECU's commands?

options.text: A manual cable directly from the power lever
The alternator field current
The VOTER switch position
An electro-mechanical actuator on the mt-Propeller P-877-16 governor

explanation: AFM 7.9.2: the ECU sets pitch via an electro-mechanical actuator on the P-877-16 governor valve, pumping gearbox oil into the propeller hub as needed.

question: Is it ever permissible to move the propeller by hand while the ENGINE MASTER switch is OFF, immediately after operation?

options.text: No — remaining pressure in the injection system rail can cause serious personal injury
Yes, this is routine and safe once the engine has stopped
Yes, but only on the RH engine
Yes, provided the ALTERNATOR switch is also OFF

explanation: AFM 4A.6.1 warns never to move the propeller by hand with ENGINE MASTER ON, and not immediately after shutdown either, due to remaining injection rail pressure.
